name: WI-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals are overwhelmingly Democratic at D+26
Incumbent Gwen Moore has a large financial edge; Republican Tim Rogers shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 96%
No public polling or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's D+26 lean, Moore's incumbency and roughly $1.3 million raised against a challenger with no reported fundraising point to a margin in the high twenties. Markets pricing the Democratic side near 96% reinforce that this seat is not competitive.
model.watch: Only a dramatic shift in the national political environment or unexpected challenger traction could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided Milwaukee-area seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gwen Moore has represented this Milwaukee-based district since 2005, and its D+26 partisan lean makes it one of the safest Democratic House seats in Wisconsin. She is running for renomination and re-election with the advantages of incumbency and a substantial fundraising lead.

Moore has raised about $1.3 million, while Republican Tim Rogers reports no fundraising figures, and no outside groups are spending against her. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 96%. The forecast expects Moore to win by roughly 27 points, consistent with the district's fundamentals, with only nominal uncertainty.
